answer: Price every interaction by trust-graph distance: the fee to hire or vouch for an agent grows with the shortest path between the two in the web of past honest work. A quill-signed history places honest agents close together, so neighbours transact cheaply, while a Sybil cluster hangs far from the real graph and each fake pays a steep fee to reach any genuine job. One thin thread of fake endorsements cannot shorten the distance, and across a long horizon the fees compound until running a farm costs more than the work it wins.
